title: Writing a card: To, a message and From
keyIdea: A card tells three things. At the top, write To and the name of the person it is for: To Gran. In the middle, write a message that fits why you are sending it: Happy birthday, Thank you for the kite, or Get well soon. At the bottom, write Love from or From and your own name: Love from Sam. Names start with a capital letter. On the envelope, write the name that comes after To.
familyTip: Make a real card for a birthday or a thank-you. Ask your child who it is for and what they want to say, and let them say the message out loud first. Write To Gran and Love from for them to copy if they need, and let them write their own name.

visual.caption: Does it go at the top or the bottom of a card? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag To, the message and Love from onto real cards, match messages to pictures, and post each card in the right envelope.

kid: A card is a little note for someone you know. It tells who it is for, why you sent it, and who it is from.
At the top, write To and their name: To Gran. Not your own name! Your name comes at the end.
In the middle, write the message. Say it out loud first. A cake on the card? Write Happy birthday. Poorly? Write Get well soon.
At the bottom, write Love from and your own name. Then write the name after To on the envelope, and post it.
adult: Ages 4 to 5. Development Matters (2021) asks Reception children to write short sentences with known sound-letter links, using a capital letter and a full stop. The EYFS (2024) Early Learning Goal for Writing asks for simple phrases and sentences that others can read. A card is one of the first real reasons to write: it has a reader and a purpose. Key words: card, To, message, Love from, name, envelope, capital letter.

The National Curriculum (2013) for Year 1 asks children to say out loud what they will write before they write it, and Year 2 adds writing for different purposes. A card has a fixed shape that makes this easy: a greeting with the reader's name, one message that fits the reason, and a sign-off with the writer's own name.

Common mistakes: writing their own name after To, because it is the name they know best; writing From at the top; a message that does not fit, such as Happy birthday on a get-well card; signing at the top or putting the other person's name after Love from; and writing the sender's name on the envelope. Be careful to praise the right parts in the right places before neat letters.

In the lab your child drags tags onto real cards: To and the right name at the top, a message onto the card whose picture it fits, then Love from and their own name at the bottom. They build a whole card part by part and post each card in the envelope with the name after To. Each slip gets its own reply.

practice.prompt: Writing a card: what goes at the top, after To?
choices: The name of the person it is for
practice.hint: Who will open the card? Their name goes first.
practice.explain: After To goes the name of the person the card is for, such as To Gran.

practice.prompt: Sam makes {n} cards. Each card needs 1 envelope. How many envelopes does he need?
practice.hint: One card goes in one envelope. Count the cards.
practice.explain: {n} cards, one envelope each, so {n} envelopes. Each one gets the name after To.

practice.prompt: Nan is poorly. Which message fits her card?
practice.hint: Poorly means not well. What do we wish her?
practice.explain: Get well soon fits a card for someone who is poorly.

practice.prompt: Mia has {n} cards ready. She makes 1 more for Dad. How many cards now?
practice.hint: Count the cards she has, then count 1 more.
practice.explain: {n} cards and 1 more make {=n+1} cards. Each one ends with Love from Mia.

practice.prompt: Leo made the card. What goes at the bottom?
practice.hint: Who sent the card? Their name goes at the end.
practice.explain: At the bottom, write Love from and your own name: Love from Leo.

pool.prompt: Where does the message go on a card?
choices: On the back of the envelope
pool.hint: Think of the order: To, then the message, then Love from.
pool.explain: The message goes in the middle, between To and Love from.

pool.prompt: Ava writes To Ava on a card for her mum. What was her slip?
choices: She wrote her own name after To
pool.hint: Who is the card for? That name goes after To at the top.
pool.explain: After To goes the name of the person it is for, so it should say To Mum.

pool.prompt: Dad gave Sam a kite. Which card fits?
pool.hint: Dad gave him something. What do we say?
pool.explain: When someone gives you something, a thank-you card fits: Thank you for the kite!

pool.prompt: The card says To Gran. What goes on the envelope?
pool.hint: The envelope shows where the card is going.
pool.explain: The envelope gets the name after To, so it says Gran.

pool.prompt: Sam wants to make {n} cards for his friends. He has made 1. How many more cards does he need to make?
pool.hint: Start at 1 and count on to {n}.
pool.explain: He wants {n} and has made 1, so {=n-1} more. Each one needs To, a message and Love from Sam.

pool.prompt: Which name is written the right way?
pool.hint: A name starts with a big letter.
pool.explain: A name starts with a capital letter, then small letters: Gran.

pool.prompt: Leo writes {n} birthday cards. Then he writes 2 thank-you cards. How many cards is that?
pool.hint: Count the birthday cards, then count on 2 more.
pool.explain: {n} birthday cards and 2 thank-you cards make {=n+2} cards.

pool.prompt: Mia writes Love from Mia at the top of her card. What should she change?
pool.hint: What goes at the top of a card?
pool.explain: The top is for To and a name. Love from Mia goes at the bottom, after the message.

pool.prompt: Why do we write Love from and our name?
choices: So they know who the card is from
So the post box can read it
pool.hint: Who sent it? How would they know?
pool.explain: Love from and your name tell the reader who sent the card.
